title: Forearm Forge
intro: Loading is what helps a sore elbow over weeks, so this is slow and light. Racket Arm, also in the Care list, is a short roll and stretch. It doesn't load the arm, and this one does.

The Take the Edge Off block is fine any day, and before you play as two holds at an RPE of 6. Do the Load It block after hitting or on a day you don't hit, at least 48 hours apart. You need a bench or table edge to rest your forearm on, and something light to hold, like a one or two kilo dumbbell or a full water bottle. If a set feels easier than a 7, slow the lowering first, and only go heavier once your elbow has been quiet the next morning. Until it settles, keep heavy carrying and gripping out of your day. If it's no better after about six weeks, see a physio, or sooner if it's getting worse or coming on earlier than it used to.

before.label: Who it's for
before.text: A sore elbow or wrist that a doctor or physio has already looked at and cleared you to train. It's built for a sore outside or inside of the elbow. If the pain is in the wrist joint itself, keep the weight in the range where it stays quiet.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: Tingling or numbness into your fingers, a grip that suddenly fails or you start dropping things, pain after a fall or a wrench, swelling, an elbow that locks or won't straighten, or pain that wakes you at night.

before.label: While you train
before.text: A bit of ache is fine. Sharp pain isn't, and neither is pain that builds through a set or feels worse the next morning. If it builds, stop that exercise. If it's sharp, stop the session.

good: Walk at an easy pace with your arms swinging
Feel your arms and hands warming up
bad: Clenching your fists as you walk

good: Make big slow circles with your arms straight out to the sides
Feel your shoulders loosen as the circles get bigger
bad: Shrugging your shoulders up to your ears

good: Make slow circles with your wrist while your forearm stays still
Feel your wrist joint moving smoothly
bad: Forcing the circle bigger than feels comfortable

good: Rest your forearm on a bench and bend your wrist up and down with nothing in your hand
Feel the muscles on both sides of your forearm warming up
bad: Bending the wrist into a pinch

good: Press your opposite thumb into the top of your forearm and slide slowly from the wrist to a hand's width below the elbow
Feel firm, steady pressure that never turns sharp
bad: Pressing on the bony point of the elbow or the sore spot beside it

exercises.name: Wrist Extension
exercises.note: Sore side. On a flared-up day, do just this block at an RPE of 6 and don't mark the session done.

good: Rest your forearm on a bench palm down and hold a light weight with your wrist up
Feel the muscles on top of your forearm working
bad: Squeezing the weight hard in your fist

exercises.name: Single-Arm Eccentric Wrist Extension
exercises.note: Sore side, 4s eccentric. If your elbow feels worse the next morning than before you started, drop one set from each exercise in this block next time, and if it's still worse after that, get it looked at.

good: Lift the weight up with your free hand, then lower it over four seconds with the wrist you're training
Feel the muscles on top of your forearm braking the lowering
bad: Dropping the weight instead of controlling it

good: Rest your forearm on a bench palm up and curl the weight up, then lower it over three seconds
Feel the muscles on the underside of your forearm working
bad: Lifting your forearm off the bench

good: Hold a light dumbbell by one end and slowly turn your palm up, then down
Feel your forearm rotating, not your elbow moving
bad: Letting your elbow swing away from your side
